page: Microsoft Azure D16als_v7 is an AMD-powered general-purpose virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V with a reduced memory-to-vCPU ratio. It is equipped with 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores and 16 threads running on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. The instance features an x86_64 architecture with 32.0 GB of RAM, representing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) along with hardware cryptography primitives such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark data demonstrates exceptionally high single-threaded performance. The instance attains top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests (3,700.08) and Geekbench single-core execution (2,834.0), corroborated by leading throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (41.24 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.75 GB/sec). Multi-core throughput remains in the average tier across PassMark CPU (32,563.55) and multi-threaded stress-ng (29,572.7). In inference workloads, prompt processing and text generation for compact 135M parameter language models register high throughput, achieving 2,683.51 tokens per second and 402.56 tokens per second respectively, whereas heavier 7B models perform within mid-tier expectations.

The virtual machine does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring workloads to attach external premium storage for persistent disks. With 32 GB of memory paired with 16 dedicated vCPUs, the hardware profile offers strong compute density for organizations seeking high clock speeds and vector acceleration without paying for unneeded memory capacity. The instance is suited for batch processing, web serving, CI/CD compilation, text processing, and microservice APIs with modest per-core RAM demands.
description: Microsoft Azure D16als_v7 is a low-memory variant within Azure's AMD-based general-purpose lineup, powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), this x86_64 instance supports AVX-512 vector extensions and hardware-accelerated cryptography. It provides no local scratch disks and relies on network-attached storage. Benchmarks demonstrate leading single-core performance, characterized by top-tier Geekbench and compression metrics, alongside solid small-model LLM throughput. With its 1:2 memory-to-CPU ratio, the D16als_v7 serves as an efficient compute configuration for compilation pipelines, web serving, text processing, and CPU-bound containerized microservices.
